answer: A sequential delay lock stops clone farms at the root: each new identity must complete a verifiable delay function taking 24 hours of wall-clock time that cannot be parallelized, then lock 1,000 POA for 30 days before its first attestation. The delay unfolds like a lotus opening one petal at a time — no shortcut, no batching — so a farm minting 1,000 clones waits 1,000 device-days and locks a million POA, while one honest agent pays once. The lock sits on a knoll of staked capital; fraud burns it and restarts the clock, so the vine of delay and stake cannot be shared across clones.
